q: Which is a structure with factory-built components that can be quickly assembled on-site?
n: A prefabricated (pre-engineered) metal building has factory-made frames, purlins and panels that are quickly assembled on site. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11 (Pre-engineered Metal Buildings).

q: Which is a two-dimensional structural system consisting of a curved steel frame that bears forces and distributes loads to the supports through its curved shape, often used for clear-span structures like bridges, warehouses and sports arenas?
n: A steel arch is a two-dimensional curved steel frame. It carries loads mainly in compression along its curve to the supports, so it suits clear spans such as bridges, warehouses and arenas. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures, Ch. 6 (Arches); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: Which is a three-dimensional structural framework made of steel elements that are interconnected in a geometric, often triangular or tetrahedral, pattern?
n: A space frame is a three-dimensional framework of linear steel members joined in a repeating geometric pattern, usually triangulated or tetrahedral. It spans in two directions. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures, Ch. 4 (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: What is the most commonly used fastener for connecting light gauge steel framing members?
n: Light-gauge steel framing is fastened mainly with self-drilling, self-tapping screws. Source: AISI S240 (Cold-Formed Steel Structural Framing); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: A steel fabricator is assembling a series of angle brackets for a mezzanine platform in a commercial warehouse. The connection requires welding two steel members that meet at a right angle, without any edge preparation, using a triangular-shaped weld deposited in the corner where the surfaces intersect. Which type of weld is most appropriate for this application?
n: A fillet weld is the triangular weld laid in the corner of members meeting at right angles, with no edge preparation. Source: AWS D1.1 (Structural Welding Code—Steel).

q: A structural-steel contractor is preparing two thick plate members for a moment-resisting beam-to-column connection in a mid-rise commercial building. The engineer requires a weld that provides full penetration, demands edge preparation before welding, and is capable of transferring high loads through the joint. Which type of weld is most appropriate for this application?
n: Groove (full-penetration) welds need edge preparation and develop the full strength of thick plates, as in moment connections. Source: AWS D1.1; AISC 360-16, Sec. J2.1.

q: A foreman reviews a fabrication drawing showing two steel plates meeting at a 90-degree angle and instructs the welder to apply the standard weld used for right-angle joints. What type of weld is typically used for this 90-degree connection?
n: The standard weld for two plates meeting at 90° is the fillet weld. Source: AWS D1.1; AISC 360-16, Sec. J2.2.

q: You placed the fastener at the upper part (crest) of a corrugated roof sheet. Which statement is correct?
o: This is preferred when the fastener lands over a purlin or batten and uses self-tapping screws with EPDM/neoprene sealing washers.
It does not matter where fasteners are placed as long as spacing is consistent.
This is never acceptable; fasteners must always go in the valley.
This is acceptable only if plain nails without washers are used.
n: Crest fastening is preferred where the screw lands on a purlin or batten and uses self-tapping screws with EPDM or neoprene washers. Water drains through the valleys, away from the hole. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing) (corrugated sheet fastening).

q: A designer is selecting a roofing system for a commercial structure exposed to strong winds and heavy rainfall. The specification requires a metal roof that uses fully concealed fasteners, minimizes horizontal joints, and allows long, uninterrupted panel runs from ridge to eave to reduce leak paths. The roof pitch is shallow, and the system must accommodate thermal movement without stressing the fasteners. Which roofing application best meets these performance requirements?
o: Low-slope metal roofing requiring concealed fasteners and long, continuous panels
Tile-profile metal roofing for steep pitches
Corrugated metal roofing with side-lap screws
High-slope metal roofing with exposed fasteners
n: Low-slope metal roofing uses concealed fasteners and long continuous panels, with few joints and room for thermal movement. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing) (structural standing-seam / low-slope metal roofing).

q: A long-span roof fora coastal commercial building requires a metal roofing system with concealed fasteners, raised interlocking vertical ribs. and the ability to accommodate thermal expansion without exposing screw penetrations. The architect specifies continuous metal panels running from ridge to cave with seams elevated above the drainage plane for superior weather-tightness. Which roofing system meets these requirements?
n: Standing seam roofing has raised interlocking ribs and concealed clips, which let panels move thermally without exposed screws. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing); MBMA Metal Roofing Systems Design Manual.

q: Which practice should be avoided when installing corrugated roofing?
o: Installing closure strips and compatible flashings at eaves and ridges
Placing exposed self-tapping screws with EPDM/neoprene washers over purlins or battens
Placing exposed nails or screws in the valley
n: Exposed fasteners in the valleys, where water runs, should be avoided because they leak. Fasten through the crests over purlins. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: A roofing component installed along the roof edge to prevent rainwater from flowing back beneath the roofing material and to direct runoff away from the fascia board is called:
n: A drip edge along the roof edge stops water creeping back under the roofing and directs runoff away from the fascia. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing) (drip edge).

q: A residential building originally used concrete roof tiles. During renovation, the architect decides to replace the roofing with long-span metal sheets. After the roof tiles are removed, which support member would most likely become immediately visible because it directly supports the tiles?
n: Roof tiles hang on battens, which are exposed as soon as the tiles are removed. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (tile roofing).

q: An architect replaces concrete roof tiles with long-span metal roofing. Which statement best describes the difference in support requirements?
o: Long-span roofing generally requires closer support spacing than roof tiles
Both systems require the same support spacing
Roof tiles generally require battens spaced more closely than the supports used for long-span roofing
Long-span roofing requires battens in addition to roof tiles
n: Roof tiles need closely spaced battens, set by the tile gauge. Long-span sheets span much farther between purlins. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: A procurement team is evaluating roofing options for a large-span training hall and must select a material that is extremely lightweight to reduce structural loading, available in factory pre-painted finishes with long-term UV stability, capable of being supplied in custom-cut lengths to eliminate end laps, and structurally suitable for true long-span roofing rather than skylight or cladding applications. Which of the following materials satisfies all of these requirements simultaneously?
n: Pre-painted long-span metal roofing is light and UV-stable, can be roll-formed to custom lengths with no end laps, and is designed for true long-span roofs. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing); MBMA Metal Roofing Systems Design Manual.

q: A campus maintenance division is retrofitting an aging steel-framed covered walkway whose existing rafters cannot support additional dead load. The new rooting must be extremely lightweight, capable of being cold-bent on site to follow a compound curved canopy profile, and easily cut into irregular shapes to fit around intersecting diagonal braces and varying bay widths. The material must withstand outdoor weathering but does not need to be pre-painted or designed for long-span structural roofing. Which material best satisfies these requirements?
n: Polycarbonate sheet is very light, can be cold-bent on site to curves, cuts easily to irregular shapes, and weathers well outdoors. Source: Manufacturer data (multiwall/solid polycarbonate); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which roofing material is traditionally used in rural areas duc to its low cost, local availability, and ability to provide natural insulation, despite requiring periodic replacement and maintenance?
n: Thatch (nipa, cogon) is cheap and locally available and insulates well, but needs periodic replacement. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; Philippine vernacular architecture (bahay kubo).

q: Which roofing material typically requires the most maintenance over time due to susceptibility to moisture. biological growth. and weathering?
n: Wood shingles need the most upkeep, being prone to moisture, rot, moss and weathering. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing) (wood shingles and shakes).

q: Roofing that lasts for 100 years or more
n: Natural slate roofs can last 100 years or more. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing) (slate roofing service life); National Slate Association.

q: A commercial building houses multiple HVAC units, exhaust fans, and water tanks on its rooftop. The maintenance team regularly walks across the roof to service equipment, requiring a surface that can safely support repeated foot traffic and concentrated loads. The structural designer must select a roofing system that demands greater structural support because of its weight and its suitability for maintenance access. If built-up roofing is not among the options, which roofing system would require the strongest structural support due to both weight and maintenance activity?
n: Of the choices, clay tile is by far the heaviest. With maintenance foot traffic, it needs the strongest supporting structure. Built-up roofing would be the ideal answer, but it is not offered. Source: ASCE 7 / NSCP 2015, Table 204-2 (roofing dead loads).

q: Which among the choices is best suited as a roof for tropical climates
n: A hip roof slopes on all four sides. It resists typhoon winds better and gives continuous eaves that shade walls from sun and rain, which suits tropical climates. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; FEMA P-499 (hip roofs and wind resistance).

q: Which two-sloped roofing style is recognized for its structural simplicity, ease of construction and effective drainage, making it the most widely used design for residential homes worldwide?
n: The gable roof, two slopes meeting at a ridge, is simple to build, drains well and is the most common residential roof. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roof forms).

q: In a long-span metal roof system. the secondary framing members must resist oa. oS bending from gravity loads while also handling moderate tension from wind uplift. o oS 2 p The section must be lightweight, economical, and allow direct fastening of roof panels without complex fabrication. Which structural shape is most appropriate for this application?
n: Cold-formed C-channels are light and economical secondary members. They resist bending and uplift and take roof fasteners directly. Source: AISI S100; NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: Most commonly used for roof purlins in light-gauge steel construction.
n: Cold-formed C-purlins (C-channels) are the most common roof purlins in light-gauge steel construction. They span between rafters or trusses to support the roofing. Source: AISI S100 (North American Specification for Cold-Formed Steel).

q: A warehouse project requires a lightweight steel structural member capable of spanning long distances between supports while carrying roof loads efficiently. Which application is most associated with steel joists?
n: Steel (open-web) joists are mainly used for long-span roofs and floors. Source: Steel Joist Institute (SJI) specifications.

q: Your client wishes to erect a house near the sea. If cost and ability to resist storms are factors to be considered, which among the following would you specify?
n: Metal roofing is economical and, properly fastened, performs well in storms. Use corrosion-resistant coatings near the sea. Source: FEMA P-499; NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: Which is a bitumen-based lightweight roofing and is moderately resistant to wind?
n: Onduline sheets are lightweight corrugated bitumen roofing with moderate wind resistance. Source: Onduline product literature.

q: Which among the following is the most economical?
n: Corrugated metal sheet is the most economical of these roofing materials. Source: Local material price indices (DPWH/PSA construction materials); NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: Which among the following is the most common roof in the country?
n: Corrugated galvanized iron is the most common roofing in the Philippines. Source: PSA Census of Population and Housing (construction materials of roof).

q: Which of the following is economical because it has a lesser risk of leaks?
n: Long-span metal roofing runs ridge to eave in one piece with no end laps, so there are fewer leak points and it costs less over time. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (roofing).

q: Which is the primary reason for maintaining a green roof il the objective is to get the most direct and measurable benefit lo a building's energy efficiency?
n: A green roof's most direct, measurable energy benefit is thermal insulation, which cuts heat gain through the roof. Source: US EPA, Reducing Urban Heat Islands—Green Roofs; FLL Green Roof Guidelines.

q: Which is an eco-friendly roofing material?
n: Clay tile is natural and recyclable, with low toxicity and long life. It is the eco-friendly choice here. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (clay tile); USGBC LEED materials guidance.

q: Which of the following roofing is the heaviest?
n: Slate is the heaviest of these roofing materials, followed by concrete and clay tiles. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-2 (roofing dead loads).

q: A flagship luxury boutique is designing a storefront where the entrance must visually disappear into a floor-to-ceiling glass facade. The brand requires a door system that maintains uninterrupted transparency. aligns flush with adjacent fixed panels, and can integrate with floor springs concealed beneath imported stone flooring. The entrance must withstand heavy foot traffic while avoiding any perimeter framing that would disrupt the minimalist retail aesthetic. Which door type best satisfies these performance and visual requirements?
n: A frameless tempered-glass swing door on concealed floor springs gives uninterrupted transparency, sits flush with fixed glass and stands up to heavy traffic. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; ASTM C1048.

q: What is the minimum standard thickness commonly used for tempered glass in framed shower enclosures?
n: Framed shower enclosures commonly use tempered glass at least 6 mm thick. Frameless ones use 10–12 mm. Source: GANA Glazing Manual (shower enclosures); ANSI Z97.1.

q: Glass that shatters into tiny safe fragments
n: Tempered glass breaks into small, blunt granular pieces. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing).

q: Glass recommended for Bathtub
n: Glass at bathtubs and showers, a hazardous location, must be safety glass, typically tempered. Source: ANSI Z97.1 / CPSC 16 CFR 1201; IBC 2406.4.5.

q: Glass recommended for high security applications such as banks.
n: Laminated glass holds together when broken and resists forced entry, which suits banks and other high-security uses. Source: ASTM F1233 (security glazing); ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing).

q: Which glass provides privacy during daylight as it makes it hard for outsiders to see inside but has the reverse effect during night Ume when the interior lights are on and its dark outside, thereby making the interior visible?
n: Reflective glass acts as a one-way mirror by day, when it is brighter outside. At night, with interior lights on, it reverses and the inside shows. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing) (reflective coated glass).

q: Architectural glazing systems enhance both aesthetics and functionality by regulating light transmission, glare and solar gain. Certain glass types utilize surface-applied coatings that diffuse light while maintaining transparency, reducing discomfort caused by excessive brightness. Which of the following is a specialty glass solution that features ceramic-based coatings fused onto its surface for glare control and solar management?
n: Fritted glass has ceramic frit fused onto its surface. It diffuses light and controls glare and solar gain. Source: GANA Glazing Manual (ceramic frit glass).

q: A commercial developer is upgrading the facade and interior partitions of a high-traffic retail space. The specification requires a safety glass that can withstand impact, break into small granular pieces rather than sharp shards, and ts suitable for doors, shower enclosures. and large storefront panels. The glass must also be four to five times stronger than ordinary annealed glass. Which type of glass meets these requirements?
n: Tempered glass is four to five times stronger than annealed and breaks into small granules. It is used in doors, showers and storefronts. Source: ASTM C1048.

q: A transportation hub is installing a large overhead skylight above a busy passenger concourse. The glazing must remain intact even if cracked, preventing pieces from falling into the occupied space below. The specification emphasizes overhead safety, fall protection, and compliance with modern building standards for public areas. Which type of glass best meets these requirements?
n: Overhead glazing over occupied areas must stay in place if cracked, so laminated glass is used. Source: IBC 2405 (Sloped Glazing and Skylights); ASTM C1172.

q: Which glass is recommended for skylights?
n: Skylights use laminated glass, whose interlayer holds fragments in place if the glass breaks. Source: IBC 2405; ASTM C1172.

q: A commercial tower is upgrading its facade to meet stricter safety and acoustic requirements. The architect specifies that the glazing must be laminated to prevent dangerous shards from falling onto sidewalks and to maintain a partial barrier even if the glass cracks. The material must also provide improved sound insulation for office tenants. Which option best describes this type of glass?
o: A composite glass made of two or more sheets bonded together with a plastic interlayer that holds fragments in place when broken
A heat-treated glass strengthened by rapid cooling to increase surface compression
A multi-layer tempered glass panel fused under high heat without any interlayer
A single sheet of annealed glass cooled slowly to minimize internal stress
n: Laminated glass is two or more sheets bonded with a plastic interlayer (PVB or SGP). It holds fragments when broken and improves sound insulation. Source: ASTM C1172.

q: A design team is evaluating glazing options for a corporate tower located directly beside an elevated railway line. The client reports persistent low-frequency vibration noise entering the interior spaces, especially during peak train hours. The facade consultant specifies that the chosen glass must improve the building's STC rating without significantly increasing overall glass thickness, and it must also function as safety glazing for a high-rise exterior. During testing, several glass types are reviewed, but only one option demonstrates the ability to dampen vibration, reduce resonance between glass layers, and maintain the impact-resistant performance required by code. Which glazing type best satisfies all of these requirements?
o: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU) with Air Gap
n: Acoustic laminated glass has a special damping interlayer. It raises STC, reduces resonance between plies, and remains safety glazing. Source: ASTM E90/E413 (STC); ASTM C1172.

q: A popular observation deck is being designed to extend from the 42nd floor of a mixed-use tower, allowing tourists to step onto a transparent glass platform and look straight down to the street below. The walkable glass surface must withstand heavy foot traffic, unpredictable crowd loads, and the possibility of objects being dropped by visitors. The design brief requires the glass to remain intact even if one or more plies fracture, ensuring that no tourist is placed at risk during a post-breakage event. The platform must also limit deflection to avoid discomfort for visitors who may be sensitive to movement at high elevation. Which glazing assembly best satisfies these requirements?
o: Double-glazed IGU with tempered outer lite
n: Walkable glass floors use triple laminated glass. The extra plies give strength, stiffness and redundancy, so the floor stays intact if one or two plies break. Source: IStructE, Structural Use of Glass in Buildings; ASTM E2751.

q: Modern glazing technologies help improve thermal efficiency. UV protection and indoor comfort without compromising clarity. Some specialized glass types feature invisible coatings that regulate heat transfer and prevent excessive solar gain. Which of the following is designed to reduce heat loss in cold climates and minimize heat gain in warm climates while maintaining maximum optical transparency?
n: Low-E glass has a nearly invisible metal-oxide coating that limits radiant heat transfer, cutting heat loss or gain while staying highly transparent. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing) (low-emissivity coatings).

q: Glass in elevator hoistway enclosures, elevator car enclosures, elevator car doors. Glass floors as a walking surface
n: Elevator hoistway and car enclosures, car doors and walkable glass floors require laminated glass. Source: ASME A17.1, Sec. 2.11/2.14 (glass in elevators); IBC 2409.

q: Which glass is used for display eases when clarity is of main concern?
n: Low-iron (extra-clear) glass has almost no green tint, giving maximum clarity for display cases. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing).

q: Which glass is used for display cases when security is of main concern?
n: Laminated glass resists break-ins and holds together, so it is used for display cases where security matters. Source: ASTM F1233.
